subject: Post-demo: function routing matrix & pilot scope
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T16:23:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: function routing matrix & pilot scope

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a proposed pilot so we can validate the architecture end-to-end: 

What we saw:
- Demo flow: user uploads invoices -> model extracts entities (structured output) -> business logic routes payment via a payments tool, with a retriever + reranker used for ambiguous vendor matches.
- We showed two function call patterns: sequential (extract -> call) and parallel candidate enrichment (call search/embedding/rerank concurrently).

Proposed pilot (4 weeks):
1) SDK and auth: Node & Java SDK integration into your staging org; we’ll configure token-based access for Hosted + service-account credentials for Dedicated if you want isolation.
2) Function definitions: canonical JSON schema for invoice_extract, vendor_lookup, payment_router. We’ll provide example tool definitions that include input schema, required scopes, and response examples.
3) Routing matrix: we’ll implement a short-circuit router so high-confidence parses go straight to payment_router; ambiguous parses trigger embeddings -> reranker -> human-in-loop.
4) Error handling & resilience: per-tool timeouts (300ms–2s depending on tool), retries with exponential backoff, idempotency keys for payment_router, and a circuit breaker for flaky vendor APIs.
5) Observability: token-level latency and per-tool logs; we’ll wire traces into your Datadog instance.

Attachments: routing_matrix_v1.xlsx (routing decision matrix), pilot_scope.md (detailed milestones + success criteria).

Ask: Can you confirm priorities (routing-first vs. embeddings-first) and whether your legal/procurement needs a staging deployment or just the Hosted proof-of-concept?

Proposed next step: 1-hour technical deep dive with your infra + security (Vivek suggested the week of July 3). Available windows: Jul 3 09:00–11:00 PT or Jul 5 14:00–16:00 PT.

Thanks —

Thanks for the clear recap, Mina — appreciate the follow-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Priority: our product team wants vendor matching to be rock-solid before anything touches payment routing. So embeddings + reranker first, then automated routing once confidence thresholds are met.
- Staging: procurement requires either a staging instance in our VPC or a dedicated sandbox with audit logs retained for 90 days. Can Redwood provide a short-term Dedicated sandbox?
- Security: we’ll need SOC 2 Type II evidence and an indication of where audit logs (who-called-what) are stored.
- Timeline: Jul 3 works for a call but our security lead is out that week. Jul 5 (afternoon PT) is better.

If you can send a brief note outlining the staging options and SOC 2 evidence, we’ll get internal sign-off.

Mina / Ben — internal technical notes to prep for Jul 5 deep dive: 

SDK & Auth:
- Offer Node and Java quickstarts (auth via short-lived tokens for Hosted; service account + KMS-wrapped keys for Dedicated sandbox). Provide sample oauth2-style flow only if they insist on that pattern; otherwise token + mTLS is simpler for their infra.

Function definitions (tool schema):
- invoice_extract: inputs = raw_pdf_base64, tenant_id; outputs = {invoices: [{vendor_id, vendor_name, amount, date, confidence}], parse_meta}.
- vendor_lookup: inputs = {vendor_name, embeddings_vector}; outputs = {candidates: [{vendor_id, score}], top_k}.
- payment_router: inputs = {vendor_id, amount, idempotency_key}; outputs = {status, tx_id}.

Parallel tool pattern recommendation:
- Kick off vendor_lookup + basic enrichment in parallel with a lightweight async embeddings pass; use a fast local model to filter obviously high-confidence cases.
- For ambiguous cases, run heavy-weight reranker sequentially to avoid charge blowup.

Error handling & resilience:
- Idempotency keys for payment_router.
- Retries: 3 attempts with exponential backoff (100ms -> 800ms) for transient HTTP 5xx from vendor APIs.
- Circuit breaker: trip after 5 consecutive failures for a given vendor endpoint for 10 minutes; fallback to manual review route.
- Timeouts: overall routing path should cap at 3s for fully automated flows; human-in-loop acceptable to 20s.

Embeddings & rerankers:
- Use a managed vector store (their preference is Pinecone — we have existing connectors).
- Persist embeddings with tenant_id prefix; set TTL 30 days for pilot.

Observability / metrics:
- Emit per-tool metrics: call_count, p95_latency, error_rate, last_success. Tag by tenant_id, routing_path, model_version.

Prep items for Jul 5:
- Ben: infra checklist (network/KMS), provide hostnames and sample firewall rules.
- Mina: get final list of Acme vendor domains so we can pre-seed vendor_lookup training set.
- I’ll draft a short runbook and share it in the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRoutingMatrix

Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
